title: Men's Rogaine 5% Solution vs Equate Minoxidil 5% Solution (3-month)

brand.product: Men's Rogaine Extra Strength 5% Minoxidil Topical Solution, Unscented, 3 x 2 fl oz (3-month supply)

alternative.product: Equate Minoxidil Topical Solution USP 5%, Extra Strength Hair Regrowth Treatment for Men, 3 x 2 fl oz (90-day)

summary: Both are 5% minoxidil topical solutions in three 2 fl oz dropper bottles, and their FDA labels list the same three inactive ingredients.
evidence: DailyMed's label for Men's Rogaine Extra Strength Unscented lists Minoxidil 5% w/v with alcohol, propylene glycol and purified water, and a 3-bottle carton (NDC 69968-0089-3). DailyMed's Equate Hair Regrowth Treatment (minoxidil solution) label, labeled by Wal-Mart, lists Minoxidil 5% w/v with alcohol, propylene glycol and purified water, a 3 x 60 mL carton (NDC 49035-746-30) and 'Compare to Men's Rogaine Extra Strength Active Ingredient'. Walmart sells both, at $49.97 ($8.33/fl oz) and $21.94 ($3.66/fl oz).
differences: We found no formula difference on the labels, only in packaging and branding. Both labels say the product is for men only, as for all 5% minoxidil solutions. Another Equate 5% 3-pack listing (item 16627518) was out of stock, but the one used here was available.

aspects.brand: 3 x 2 fl oz (60 mL) bottles, 3-month supply
aspects.alternative: 3 x 2 fl oz (60 mL) dropper bottles, 90-day

aspects.alternative: FDA drug label on DailyMed, NDC 49035-746

why: Both are 5% minoxidil in alcohol, propylene glycol and purified water, in three 2 fl oz dropper bottles, and the DailyMed labels list the same three inactives. The record finds no formula difference, only in packaging and branding.

title: Women's Rogaine 2% Solution vs Equate Minoxidil 2% for Women (3-month)

brand.product: Women's Rogaine 2% Minoxidil Hair Regrowth Solution, Unscented, 3 x 2 fl oz (3-month supply)

alternative.product: Equate Minoxidil Topical Solution 2%, Hair Regrowth Treatment for Women, 3 x 2 fl oz (3-month)

summary: Both are 2% minoxidil topical solutions for women, sold as three 2 fl oz bottles for a three-month supply.
evidence: DailyMed's Women's Rogaine Unscented solution label lists Minoxidil 2% w/v (alcohol, propylene glycol, purified water) and a 3-bottle carton (NDC 69968-0090-3). Walmart's Equate listing states Minoxidil 2%, twice-daily use with an enclosed dropper, and says it 'can be compared to the active ingredient in Women's Rogaine'. At $3.82 per fl oz, Walmart's price works out to the full 6 fl oz 3-pack at $22.94, against $49.99 for Rogaine's 3-pack.
differences: We could not see Equate's printed Drug Facts or inactive ingredients, so we have not confirmed that its base is the same alcohol, propylene glycol and water mix as Rogaine's. That is why confidence is medium. This pair covers only the 2% twice-daily liquid, not Women's Rogaine 5% once-daily foam.

aspects.brand: Full Drug Facts on DailyMed, incl. inactives
aspects.alternative: Online listing shows only active and strength

title: Listerine Cool Mint vs Equate Antiseptic Mouthwash Blue Mint 1.5 L

brand.product: Listerine Cool Mint Antiseptic Mouthwash, 1.5 L (50.7 fl oz)

alternative.product: Equate Antiseptic Mouthwash, Blue Mint, 1.5 L (50.7 fl oz)

summary: Equate Blue Mint has the same four essential-oil actives at the same strengths as Listerine Cool Mint, and the same inactive ingredients, for under half the price.
evidence: DailyMed's Listerine Cool Mint Antiseptic label lists eucalyptol 0.092%, menthol 0.042%, methyl salicylate 0.060% and thymol 0.064%. Its inactives are water, alcohol (21.6%), sorbitol, poloxamer 407, benzoic acid, sodium saccharin, sodium benzoate, flavor and green 3. The FDA label for Equate Antiseptic Mouthwash Blue Mint (NDC 49035-664, distributed by Wal-Mart, 1.5 L) lists the same actives at the same percentages and the same inactives with 21.6% alcohol, and says 'Compare to Cool Mint Listerine'. Walmart's Equate page also says it is accepted by the American Dental Association.
differences: The flavor is called Blue Mint rather than Cool Mint, and the flavoring blend isn't disclosed, so the taste may differ slightly. The inactive list is printed in a slightly different order. Listerine averages 0.1 star higher at Walmart. For bulk buyers, Walmart's 6-bottle Listerine quantity option was $25.18 (8.3¢/fl oz) when we checked, close to Equate's 7.9¢, so the saving mostly applies to single bottles.

aspects.brand: Water, 21.6% alcohol, sorbitol, poloxamer 407, benzoates, saccharin, flavor, green 3

aspects.alternative: Blue Mint (sold as compare to Cool Mint)

why: Both have the same four essential-oil actives at the same strengths and the same inactive list, including 21.6% alcohol. The Equate is Blue Mint rather than Cool Mint, so the taste may differ slightly, and Walmart's six-bottle Listerine price was close to Equate's per ounce, so the saving mostly applies to single bottles.

title: CeraVe Acne Control Cleanser vs up&up Oil Free Acne Wash 2% Salicylic Acid

brand.product: CeraVe Acne Control Face Cleanser with 2% Salicylic Acid, 8 fl oz

alternative.product: up&up Oil Free Acne Wash with Salicylic Acid, 8 fl oz

summary: Both are 2% salicylic acid acne washes with the same ceramide, niacinamide and hectorite-clay base, and Target's up&up costs less than half as much per ounce.
evidence: CeraVe's own product page lists Salicylic Acid 2% with water, sodium lauroyl sarcosinate, cocamidopropyl hydroxysultaine, glycerin, niacinamide, gluconolactone, ceramides NP/AP/EOP, cholesterol, hectorite, phytosphingosine and other ingredients. Target's up&up label lists salicylic acid 2.0% with ceramides AP/EOP/NP, cholesterol, cocamidopropyl hydroxysultaine, gluconolactone, hectorite, niacinamide, phytosphingosine, sodium lauroyl sarcosinate and sodium methyl cocoyl taurate. Walmart sells CeraVe's 8 fl oz for $14.24 ($1.78/fl oz). Target sells up&up's 8 fl oz for $5.99 ($0.75/fl oz).
differences: The inactive lists overlap heavily but aren't identical. CeraVe's current formula adds calcium gluconate, triethyl citrate, tetrasodium EDTA, hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid and trisodium ethylenediamine disuccinate. up&up instead has PEG-6 caprylic/capric glycerides, sodium citrate, sodium chloride, tetrasodium glutamate diacetate and hyaluronic acid. up&up doesn't claim to copy CeraVe, is sold only at Target, and has fewer and lower reviews.

aspects.brand: Ceramides NP/AP/EOP, cholesterol, niacinamide, hectorite clay
aspects.alternative: Ceramides NP/AP/EOP, cholesterol, niacinamide, hectorite clay

aspects.brand: Adds calcium gluconate, triethyl citrate, EDTA, hydrolyzed HA
aspects.alternative: Adds PEG-6 glycerides, sodium citrate, salt, hyaluronic acid

why: Both list 2% salicylic acid with the same ceramides, cholesterol, niacinamide and hectorite clay, in 8 fl oz. The full inactive lists differ in a few ingredients, and the record shows no test where the CeraVe performs better.

title: CeraVe Acne Foaming Cream Cleanser 4% BP vs up&up Benzoyl Peroxide Acne Cleanser

brand.product: CeraVe Acne Foaming Cream Cleanser with 4% Benzoyl Peroxide, Hyaluronic Acid, Niacinamide, 5 fl oz

alternative.product: up&up Benzoyl Peroxide Acne Cleanser 4%, 5 fl oz

summary: Both are 4% benzoyl peroxide acne cleansers built on ceramides, niacinamide and hyaluronic acid, and up&up costs about half as much per ounce.
evidence: Walmart's and Target's CeraVe listings state 4% benzoyl peroxide, and Walmart's title names hyaluronic acid and niacinamide. Walmart's search listing priced the 5 fl oz at $14.97 ($2.99/fl oz). Target's up&up label lists benzoyl peroxide 4.0% with ceramides AP/EOP/NP, cholesterol, niacinamide, phytosphingosine, sodium hyaluronate, glycerin and glycolic acid, at $7.99 ($1.60/fl oz).
differences: We did not see CeraVe's full inactive list on the pages we checked, so the formulas are matched on the active and the headline skin-barrier ingredients, not line by line. Target's title says 5.5 oz but its specs and unit price indicate 5 fl oz. up&up is Target-only, has far fewer reviews, and makes no 'compare to CeraVe' claim. Benzoyl peroxide can bleach fabrics with either product.
